headline: India Oil Bill Surges 46% as State Absorbs 1.7% of GDP to Shield Fuel Consumers
summary: India's crude oil import bill surged 46% in September, with the public sector absorbing an estimated 1.7% of GDP to insulate domestic consumers from elevated global crude prices.
why: India imports over 80% of its crude requirements, making international oil shocks a primary factor in its fiscal deficit and current account stability.

impacts.name: India
impacts.why: Absorbing rising international fuel costs increases public sector fiscal burdens and widens import expenditure.
